description: Study-level extraction. Values transcribed from user-provided full-text PDFs with exact provenance. Sources not provided remain pending_full_text. Small-molecule vs nanoparticle status flagged per study (critical: the provided skin studies are small-molecule, not nanoparticle).

free_dox_caveat.reviewer_conclusion: mass-balance approach may not yield reliable free-doxorubicin estimates

extracted_values.bilayer: liquid-ordered phase, high-Tm (53 C) HSPC + cholesterol

extracted_values.targeting: passive (EPR); extravasation via porous tumour capillaries permeable to particles <=100 nm

secondary_PK.label: UNVERIFIED_SECONDARY

secondary_tumour.label: UNVERIFIED_SECONDARY

studies.identity: Chen Y et al. Int J Nanomedicine 2012;7:3023-3033 (batch-2 duplicate upload re-mined for full composition).

composition_Table1_mg.note: charge set by primary lipid/modifier: cationic=stearylamine(+), neutral=glyceryl behenate, anionic=Precirol ATO-5; solid:liquid lipid = 3:1; +Pluronic F68 aqueous; 15 mg tripterine

extracted_values.prep_method: solvent evaporation (drug + lipids dissolved in acetone/ethanol, added to aqueous Pluronic F68)
extracted_values.release_method: dialysis (MWCO 8,000-14,000), receptor 2:8 ethanol:PBS pH 7.4, 37 C, sink
extracted_values.release_interpretation: APPARENT (dialysis-membrane-coupled) release, NOT pure carrier-release kinetics - the membrane and dissolution steps are convolved
extracted_values.permeation_method: Sprague-Dawley RAT full-thickness abdominal skin, Franz cell, receptor 2:8 ethanol:PBS pH 7.4, 400 rpm, 37 C

studies.identity: Huang K, Ma H, Liu J, Huo S, Kumar A, Wei T, Zhang X, Jin S, Gan Y, Wang PC, He S, Zhang X, Liang X-J. Size-Dependent Localization and Penetration of Ultrasmall Gold Nanoparticles in Cancer Cells, Multicellular Spheroids, and Tumors in Vivo. ACS Nano 2012;6(5):4483-4493.
studies.api_class: NANOPARTICLE (gold, intact carrier) - NO API, NO drug release

extracted_values.zeta_mV: -23.8 to -35.3 (paper prints 'eV', typo for mV); more negative for larger NP
extracted_values.uptake: ICP-MS gold-atom concentration per cell (QUANTITATIVE): smaller NPs -> more Au per cell
extracted_values.spheroid_penetration: SEMI-QUANTITATIVE (dark-field + TEM imaging): 2 and 6 nm penetrate deeply into spheroid core and reach cytoplasm+nucleus; 15 nm stays peripheral
extracted_values.in_vivo: ICP-MS tumour accumulation after single IV (n=3); higher tumour accumulation / deeper localization for 2-6 nm

studies.endpoint_types: total cellular uptake = quantitative (ICP-MS); radial/spatial penetration = semi-quantitative imaging (NOT concentration-vs-radius)
studies.limitations: no exact concentration-vs-radius profile (imaging only); MCF-7 single line; no API payload; SI (Figs S1-S3) not provided; no independent external validation
studies.note: Upgrades Profile C from illustrative-only to a RESEARCH-SUPPORTED size-dependent intact-carrier penetration benchmark. Do NOT convert imaging to exact concentration profiles; do NOT infer API release.

studies.identity: Li Y, Qi L, Wang Y, Li Y, Lei C, Zhang Y, ... Wang X. A multicenter randomized trial to compare the bioequivalence and safety of a generic doxorubicin hydrochloride liposome injection with Caelyx in advanced breast cancer. Front Oncol 2022;12:1070001.

design.reference: Caelyx (Janssen-Cilag International NV, Belgium) - EU twin of Doxil, 20 mg/10 mL

studies.free_dox_assay: DIRECTLY assayed: free doxorubicin separated by solid-phase extraction (SPE); encapsulated pretreated separately (NOT total-minus-encapsulated mass balance)

extracted_values.unit_caveat: paper prints AUC/Cmax of encapsulated as 'mg/mL' but context (and consistency with the DOXIL label) indicates ug/mL; transcribed verbatim with this note
extracted_values.BE_conclusion: all 90% CIs within 80-125% for both free and encapsulated -> bioequivalent

studies.compatibility_assessment: reference arm = Caelyx = Janssen EU twin of Doxil (same formulation) -> Caelyx values directly applicable to Profile E; test (generic) shown bioequivalent. Grade DIRECT_PARTIAL for Profile E (Caelyx reference, different trial than the US label).
studies.resolves_fda_uncertainty: provides directly-measured (SPE) free-dox PK, more defensible than the FDA S-050 mass-balance estimate (which gave 42% negative values). Does not merge free/encapsulated; keeps them separate.
studies.note: Key new Profile-E evidence for the FREE-vs-ENCAPSULATED module. Systemic PK only - NO tumour tissue distribution.

studies.identity: Cern A, Golbraikh A, Sedykh A, Tropsha A, Barenholz Y, Goldblum A. Quantitative structure-property relationship modeling of remote liposome loading of drugs. J Control Release 2012;160(2):147-157.
studies.type: QSPR / machine-learning modeling (Profile E mechanistic support ONLY)

extracted_values.validation: 5-fold external validation; binary + continuous ML models; high external prediction accuracy
extracted_values.mechanism: remote loading of amphipathic weak bases/acids via transmembrane ammonium-sulfate / pH gradient; requires a logD window
extracted_values.doxorubicin_specific: doxorubicin present in dataset (6 mentions) but per-drug loading values are in SI (not provided)

studies.not_evidence_for: Doxil release kinetics, plasma PK, tumour penetration, intratumoral release
studies.note: Supports the remote-loading formulation module qualitatively; do NOT use as direct Doxil release/PK data.
